title: 8 Best Daily Affirmation Apps for iPhone in 2026 (Free & Paid), Tested
description: The best daily affirmation apps in 2026, tested and compared: I am +, I am, Mantra, Self Love, Vision Board ++, Gratitude, Motivation and Anicca, verified against US App Store listings read in October and November 2026.
markdown:
By Anicca · November 2026

Updated November 2026

Key takeaways

- **Best free, ad-free affirmation app:** I am + — custom affirmations, AI affirmations and practice sessions with music and voices are free; $4/yr unlocks more AI topics, voices and your own music.
- **Biggest affirmation library:** I am — 4.8 stars from over 1.2 million ratings across all storefronts and many categories; the free version shows a lot of ads, Premium costs $60/yr.
- **Affirmations with a vision board:** Vision Board ++ — turns your board and affirmations into a slideshow with music and spoken affirmations, plus a gratitude journal; 4.9 stars, $19/yr.
- **Affirmations in your own voice:** Mantra — record your affirmations and practise them in guided sessions, about $30/yr.
- **Affirmations with a gratitude journal:** Gratitude — journaling first, with affirmations and a vision board section, about $30/yr.

Pick one app and open it every day: a few minutes of daily practice does more than the biggest library you never use. For the wider field compared by what each app lets you do with the words, see our [full guide to the best affirmation apps](https://aniccaai.com/blog/best-affirmation-apps-2026-11-05), and for the gratitude side of the same practice, see our [guide to the best gratitude journal apps](https://aniccaai.com/blog/best-gratitude-journal-apps-2026-11-17).

Affirmation apps put short, positive statements in front of you every day: as reminders, widgets, read-aloud sessions or recordings in your own voice. This page follows a tested comparison of seven iPhone apps in which each app was installed and used — own affirmations written, sessions, reminders and widgets tried, and the free plan checked for what it really includes. We make Anicca, added eighth here and scored with the same rubric as every other app, and we do not rank it first. The makers of the comparison this page follows make I am + and Vision Board ++, and score their own apps the same way.

Prices, ratings and platforms come from each app's US App Store listing. The comparison this page follows checked them on 22 October 2026, with rating counts summed across all 175 App Store storefronts; we re-checked the US listings on 18 November 2026 and note the current US counts in each section where they differ. Prices change — check the store before you subscribe.

## What to look for in an affirmation app

Six checks separate an app you keep using from one you forget after a week:

- **Free plan and ads.** Can you write and practise your own affirmations for free, without ads?
- **Your own words.** Can you add your own affirmations and sort them into collections?
- **Audio.** Are there sessions with voices and music, or can you record your own voice?
- **Daily reminders.** Do reminders and home-screen or lock-screen widgets keep an affirmation in view?
- **AI affirmations.** Can the app write affirmations for your own situation?
- **Focus.** Do you want affirmations only, or a journal or vision board next to them?

## Best Daily Affirmation Apps 2026

### 1. I am +: Best free, ad-free affirmation app

**Best for:** anyone who wants personal, AI-made affirmations and calm practice sessions, with no ads and no paywall for the basics.

**Not for:** Android users, or people who want a journal in the same app.

**Price** (US App Store, checked Oct 2026): Free, no ads; $4 per year or $1 per month for the extras

**Free trial:** none needed · **Rating:** 4.8 stars · **Ratings:** 101 across all storefronts (27 in the US on 18 November 2026, as I am + AI Affirmations Widget by Hero21)

Type any wish, such as wanting to feel more confident, and I am + writes a set of personal affirmations with AI. Add your own, sort them into collections and get reminders through the day. All of that is free and ad-free.

Sessions turn your list into a short daily practice: the app reads your affirmations aloud in one of several voices over calm music. Home-screen and lock-screen widgets keep a line in view, and streaks show how often you practised. For $4 a year you get more AI topics, more voices and your own music.

**✓ Pros**

- Custom affirmations, collections and reminders for free
- AI affirmations for any topic
- Sessions with voices and music
- Home-screen and lock-screen widgets
- No ads; $4 a year for the extras

**✗ Considerations**

- iPhone and iPad only (no Android)
- No journal or Apple Watch app
- Fewer fonts and colours than some rivals

**Verdict:** The easiest way to start a daily affirmation habit: the core app is free and ad-free, and the extras cost $4 a year.

### 2. I am: Best for the biggest affirmation library

**Best for:** ready-made affirmations in many categories, delivered as reminders all day.

**Not for:** anyone who dislikes ads and does not want to pay for Premium.

**Price** (US App Store, checked Oct 2026): Free with ads; Premium $60 per year, $15 per month or $150 lifetime

**Free trial:** 3 days · **Rating:** 4.8 stars · **Ratings:** 1,243,596 across all storefronts (739,486 in the US on 18 November 2026, version 7.9.0, updated 12 November 2026)

I am, by Monkey Taps, has been on the App Store since 2014 and has by far the most ratings of any app in this list. You pick intentions and categories, and the app sends matching affirmations as reminders through the day; widgets, an Apple Watch app and many themes keep them in view. It is also available on Android.

The free version shows a lot of ads; Premium removes them and unlocks all categories, themes and more reminders.

**✓ Pros**

- Very large library across many categories
- Reminders, widgets and Apple Watch
- AI affirmations
- iPhone, iPad and Android

**✗ Considerations**

- Many ads in the free version
- Highest yearly price in this list ($60)
- No journal

**Verdict:** The best-known affirmation app with a very large library; plan on Premium if ads bother you.

### 3. Mantra: Best for affirmations in your own voice

**Best for:** hearing your affirmations in your own voice and in short guided sessions.

**Not for:** a full free tier: most categories and your own affirmations need Premium.

**Price** (US App Store, checked Oct 2026): Free; Premium about $30 per year (yearly plans from $15 to $60 are listed), $5 per month or $75 lifetime

**Free trial:** 7 days · **Rating:** 4.8 stars · **Ratings:** 76,367 in the comparison this page follows (a US search on 18 November 2026 surfaced a different app also named Mantra at 34,485 ratings, so treat this count as the followed comparison's October 2026 figure)

Mantra has over a thousand "I am" affirmations in more than 30 categories. Record your own voice and play affirmations on repeat, or follow guided and manifestation sessions with ambient sounds. Smart reminders arrive in the morning, during the day and at bedtime, widgets show an affirmation on your home screen, and themes with backgrounds, videos and fonts change the look.

The free version covers the general category. In the followed comparison's test, reminders sometimes had to be switched off and on again before they fired.

**✓ Pros**

- Record affirmations in your own voice
- Guided and manifestation sessions
- 1,000+ affirmations in 30+ categories
- Morning, daytime and bedtime reminders

**✗ Considerations**

- Most categories need Premium
- Ads during sessions in the free version
- Occasional bugs in the followed test

**Verdict:** The strongest pick for practising in your own voice, at about $30 a year.

### 4. Self Love: Best for mirror practice

**Best for:** saying affirmations out loud while you see yourself (Mirror Mode), in 1-, 3- or 5-minute sessions.

**Not for:** AI affirmations or your own music.

**Price** (US App Store, checked Oct 2026): Free; $14 per year (a $7.99 one-year plan is also listed), $4 per month or $60 lifetime

**Free trial:** 3 days · **Rating:** 4.8 stars · **Ratings:** 2,388 in the comparison this page follows (2,053 in the US on 18 November 2026, version 7.3, updated 5 November 2026)

Self Love pairs daily affirmations and uplifting quotes with Mirror Mode, which shows your camera image while you say each affirmation out loud. Sessions of 1, 3 or 5 minutes can be read or listened to, with calming sounds. Home-screen and lock-screen widgets, an Apple Watch app, streaks and affirmation wallpapers keep the practice going.

The free version covers general topics and your favourites; the full category list and themes need Premium.

**✓ Pros**

- Mirror Mode for saying affirmations out loud
- Short read-or-listen sessions
- Widgets, Apple Watch and streaks
- Low yearly price

**✗ Considerations**

- General topics only in the free version
- No AI affirmations
- No own music

**Verdict:** A calm, well-designed app for a short daily ritual, at about $14 a year.

### 5. Vision Board ++: Best for affirmations with a vision board

**Best for:** people who want their affirmations next to their goals: a vision board, a movie of it with music and spoken affirmations, and a gratitude journal.

**Not for:** Android users.

**Price** (US App Store, checked Oct 2026): Free; $19 per year, $5 per month or $3 per week for the extras

**Free trial:** 3 days · **Rating:** 4.9 stars · **Ratings:** 9,603 across all storefronts (3,095 in the US on 18 November 2026, as Vision Board ++ Maker Manifest by Hero21)

Vision Board ++ has a full affirmation tab: thousands of affirmations in many categories, your own affirmations in collections, AI affirmations for any wish, and sessions with many voices, music or your own recorded voice.

What sets it apart is the vision board. Build boards from your photos or a large image library, and every board becomes a short movie with music and spoken affirmations. Widgets, lock-screen widgets, a gratitude journal, a PIN lock and iCloud sync come with it.

**✓ Pros**

- Affirmations, sessions and AI affirmations in one app
- Record affirmations in your own voice
- Vision board movie with music and spoken affirmations
- Widgets, gratitude journal and iCloud sync

**✗ Considerations**

- iPhone and iPad only (no Android)
- More features than you need for affirmations alone
- No Apple Watch app

**Verdict:** The best choice if you want to see your goals and hear your affirmations in one daily ritual, for $19 a year.

### 6. Gratitude: Best for a gratitude journal with affirmations

**Best for:** journaling first, with affirmations and a vision board on the side.

**Not for:** built-in voices: spoken affirmations need your own recording.

**Price** (US App Store, checked Oct 2026): Free; $30 per year or $5 per month (a $39.99 "Gratitude Pro" option is also listed)

**Free trial:** 7 days · **Rating:** 4.9 stars · **Ratings:** 91,810 in the comparison this page follows (44,994 in the US on 18 November 2026, version 6.0.3, updated 7 November 2026)

Gratitude, by Hapjoy, is a journal app at heart: daily prompts, photos and voice notes in your entries, journaling streaks and guided challenges. Its affirmation section has hundreds of affirmations; you can write your own, add music, record your voice and play or shuffle a collection. A vision board section turns your goals into a video with music. It is also available on Android.

More sounds and session settings need Pro, and there is no built-in voice to read affirmations aloud.

**✓ Pros**

- Full gratitude journal with prompts and streaks
- Your own affirmations with voice recording
- Vision board section with video
- iPhone, iPad and Android

**✗ Considerations**

- Affirmations are a side feature
- No built-in voices
- More sounds and session settings need Pro

**Verdict:** The pick for a journaling habit with affirmations on the side, at $30 a year. For a dedicated comparison of this side of the practice, see our [guide to the best gratitude journal apps](https://aniccaai.com/blog/best-gratitude-journal-apps-2026-11-17).

### 7. Motivation: Best for daily quotes instead of "I am" statements

**Best for:** short motivational quotes on your home screen and in reminders.

**Not for:** classic "I am" affirmations, sessions or audio.

**Price** (US App Store, checked Oct 2026): Free with ads; Premium plans listed from $3.99 to $47.99 (the store does not name their periods)

**Free trial:** 3 days · **Rating:** 4.8 stars · **Ratings:** 1,964,020 in the comparison this page follows (1,080,373 in the US on 18 November 2026, version 7.9.0, updated 13 November 2026)

Motivation, from the makers of I am, sends quotes from authors, athletes and thinkers instead of first-person affirmations. Thousands of quotes are sorted into topics such as self-esteem, stress, work and love; save favourites, change fonts and colours and share quotes as images. Widgets and a weekly streak keep a quote in front of you. It is also available on Android.

The free version shows ads; Premium removes them and unlocks all themes, categories and unlimited reminders.

**✓ Pros**

- Very large quote library by topic
- Home-screen widgets and reminders
- Share quotes as images
- iPhone, iPad and Android

**✗ Considerations**

- Quotes, not "I am" affirmations
- Ads in the free version
- No audio or sessions

**Verdict:** A good daily nudge if you prefer quotes to affirmations.

### 8. Anicca: Best for one short card, and nothing else to manage (our app)

**Best for:** one short, believable affirmation card on your iPhone Lock Screen every day, chosen from the topics you picked at setup, with no streak to keep up.

**Not for:** Android users, or anyone who wants a journal, a vision board, voice recording or a large library to browse.

**Price** (US App Store and product page, checked 18 November 2026): Free to download; Anicca Premium $59.99 per year unlocks the full library

**Free trial:** 3 days · **Rating:** 5.0 stars · **Ratings:** 1 in the US (version 1.9.14, updated 13 November 2026)

Anicca is our own app, and it is the narrowest option on this list by design. You choose what you are struggling with during setup, enable notifications, and receive short cards to read, including a new affirmation on your Lock Screen every day. There are swipeable cards, favourites and widgets, and there are deliberately no streaks to keep up. It requires iOS 16.6 or later, and its topics are written for difficult days — self-criticism, overthinking and anxiety among them — in short, believable lines rather than grand claims. Read more on [Anicca's product page](https://aniccaai.com/affirmation-app).

That narrowness is the whole tradeoff, stated plainly. Anicca has no Android version, no voice recording, no journal, no vision board and no AI affirmation generator. Its public store reach is also the smallest here by a wide margin: 5.0 stars from 1 rating on the US App Store on 18 November 2026. If you want scale, a library to browse or a voice practice, the apps above fit better.

**✓ Pros**

- One short card a day, with nothing else to manage
- Topics chosen for difficult days, in believable lines
- Lock Screen delivery, notifications, swipeable cards and widgets
- No streaks to keep up

**✗ Considerations**

- iPhone only (no Android, no iPad focus)
- No journal, vision board, voice recording or AI generation
- Smallest store reach on this list (1 US rating)

**Verdict:** Choose Anicca when the other formats have already become background noise and what you want is one short card, at the moment you pick up your phone, with nothing else to maintain. Choose I am + for a free ad-free start, I am for the established library, or Gratitude for a journal.

## How we choose the best daily affirmation apps

We compared the apps on the same criteria: price and ads, ease of use, the affirmation library, your own and AI affirmations, sessions and audio, reminders and widgets, extras such as a journal or vision board, and platforms. The followed comparison's hands-on use of each of the first seven apps is complemented by public App Store data; Anicca is our own app, described from its product page and store listing.

### Ratings-count methodology

For rows 1–7, rating counts (for example 9,603 for Vision Board ++) are the sum of App Store ratings across all 175 App Store storefronts, pulled on 22 October 2026 by the comparison this page follows, using the same method for every app. Star ratings are the US App Store averages. I am + is the newest app among the seven and rests on 101 ratings (26 in the US at that check, 27 on 18 November 2026), so its average can still move. Where we re-checked a US listing on 18 November 2026, the current US count is given in that app's section. Anicca's count is US-only and is not summed across storefronts.

### Prices, trials and platforms

Prices are the in-app purchases listed on each app's US App Store page. Free-trial lengths are shown inside the apps, not on the store, so for rows 1–7 they come from the followed comparison's tests and can change. An app counts as available on Android when a Google Play listing was found.

### Selection criteria

- **Price** — free plan, ads, subscription or lifetime cost.
- **Usability** — how quickly you can write and practise your first affirmation.
- **Creation** — built-in library, your own affirmations, collections, AI affirmations.
- **Customization** — backgrounds, fonts, colours, voices and music.
- **Practice** — sessions, own-voice recording, reminders, widgets, streaks.
- **Extras** — journal, vision board, Apple Watch.
- **Sync** — iPad support and syncing between devices.
- **Ratings** — App Store rating and all-storefront rating count (see above).

### Disclosure

We make Anicca, added eighth here; the comparison this page follows is published by the makers of I am + and Vision Board ++ (mHero21 e.U.). To counter-balance that, every app is scored from the same public App Store data and against the same rubric. Where a competitor is the better fit for a specific need, we say so — including in Anicca's own section above.

## Frequently asked questions

### What is the best free affirmation app?

I am + is the best free affirmation app in the followed test: the free version has no ads and covers the basics, including your own affirmations, collections, reminders, widgets and AI affirmations, and you can practise them in sessions with voices and music. A $4-a-year plan adds more AI topics, more voices and your own music. Among the other apps, Self Love and Mantra have usable free versions limited to general topics, and I am is free with a lot of ads. Anicca is free to download, with its full library behind Anicca Premium at $59.99 a year.

### What is the best free affirmation app for iPad?

I am + runs natively on iPad and its free version is ad-free, so it is the followed comparison's pick for iPad as well. The first seven apps in this review run on iPad; Vision Board ++ is the choice if you also want a vision board on the larger screen, and Gratitude if you prefer journaling. Anicca is an iPhone app.

### Which affirmation apps let you record your own voice?

Mantra, Vision Board ++ and Gratitude let you record affirmations in your own voice and play them back. I am + and I am read affirmations aloud with built-in voices instead, and Self Love has you say them out loud in Mirror Mode. Anicca does not offer recording; its cards are read, not listened to.

### Which affirmation apps have home-screen widgets?

Six of the first seven apps have home-screen widgets: I am +, I am, Mantra, Self Love, Vision Board ++ and Motivation. I am + and Self Love also offer lock-screen widgets, and I am and Self Love have Apple Watch apps. Gratitude does not list a widget in the followed comparison. Anicca also offers widgets, including a new affirmation on your Lock Screen every day.

### Do affirmation apps actually work?

Affirmations can help, but they are not magic. Studies on self-affirmation, where you reflect on values that matter to you, show lower stress and more openness to change (Cohen & Sherman, 2014) and activity in brain regions linked to self-related processing and reward (Cascio et al., 2016). Repeating overly positive statements can backfire for people with low self-esteem (Wood, Perunovic & Lee, 2009). Affirmations that are specific and believable, practised daily and tied to action work best, and an app helps mainly by keeping them in front of you. An affirmation app is not a substitute for professional mental-health care, diagnosis or treatment.
